title: A year into development, I'd love you opinion on my AI assisted development journey
author: ObjectiveBank1903
selftext:
Hello everyone!  


A little over a year ago I started development on my first ever game, Gamarra - Street Vendor Simulator.   
  
The game is set in Peru's largest market and I chose it because I wanted to share with the world a bit of what entrepreneurship looks like in a developing country.  
  
I used AI to help me write the code, generate 2D art, while the 3D assets were modeled by  me in Blender, and some are from the store. I have a day job unrelated to game dev so I worked on this project nights and weekends. I built the game entirely in Unity.  


My Steam page has been live for about a month now and wishlist conversion has been lower than I expected. There are probably many reasons for this: the release date is still far away, there is no demo yet, and I know AI usage creates strong opinions.

I'm prepared for the possibility that this game may not meet my financial expectations, but I still want to make it the best game I can.

  
So I'd genuinely love your feedback:

* What is your impression when you see the Steam page?
* Are the trailer and screenshots good?
* What would make you more interested in this project?



A year ago I never imagined I would be able to build and share something like this. Thanks to AI tools, I'm getting closer to releasing my first demo..  


Thanks and I appreciate your feedback, here is the  link to my page  


[https://store.steampowered.com/app/4535020/Gamarra\_\_Street\_Vendor\_Simulator/?utm\_source=reddit&utm\_medium=post&utm\_campaign=redditai](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4535020/Gamarra__Street_Vendor_Simulator/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=redditai)

comments.author: riverbronze
comments.body:
The cover image undersold the game. It has that very AI generated feel.

And then the game itself looks awesome.

I strongly recommend you to just swap the cover and go for a vivid, flat art style.

replies.author: ObjectiveBank1903
replies.body: Fair point, I will look into it, thank you

comments.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
comments.body: I love how colorful it is

replies.author: ObjectiveBank1903
replies.body: Thanks, it's complicated to capture the chaos of real Gamarra. I'm still working hard at adding props while keeping the geometry low

replies.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
replies.body: Yeah I looked at pictures of real Gamarra and it’s certainly grimier. It’s a video game though and I liked the colors. Making it more chaotic would be nice.

comments.author: Am_Biyori
comments.body:
Congratulations! This is the first AI built game I've seen on Reddit that actually looks fun to play. You did a good job on the steam page too. Smart move using trailers to show features rather than just describing them.

As you get closer to finishing, remember what they say- 80% of the work goes into the last 20% of the game. Work hard on making sure every interaction and character movement is satisfying. Can't for the demo.

replies.author: ObjectiveBank1903
replies.body: Indeed, I am polishing the demo now and I find a bunch of small details to polish. I aim to have the demo around July

comments.author: macobits
comments.body:
Oh LOL! As as peruvian I can totally see the whole charm on this 😁😁😁 Very good job! It has also the same vibe as many simulators in Steam.

My only thing would be to take some more work on the UI for Menus / Dialogs. But overall, wish you good luck!

replies.author: ObjectiveBank1903
replies.body: Thanks, I am peruvian too. I'll localize the steam page soon, and the game after the demo

comments.author: Similar_Cook1055
comments.body: Keep up the good work , I would wishlist it

replies.author: ObjectiveBank1903
replies.body: Thank you, it means a lot
